corrected_record.support_text: FIAU, a nucleoside fluorinated in the carbohydrate moiety used against hepatitis B virus, caused unanticipated lethal toxicity in HBV-infected patients after 8-12 weeks of treatment. Paragraph 40 adds that mitochondrial toxicity has been suggested to play a key role in this FIAU-causing liver failure, with evidence in FIAU-treated patients including severe lactic acidosis and massive macro- and microvesicular steatosis in liver biopsies, plus enlarged and irregular mitochondria on electron micrographs.
corrected_record.qualifying_conditions: Observed in HBV-infected patients; lethal toxicity appeared after 8-12 weeks of treatment for hepatitis B virus infection.
corrected_record.extra_details: FIAU (fluoro-arabinofuranosyl uracil) is a nucleoside analog; its 5'-triphosphate (FIAU-TP) is the likely active metabolite formed by host thymidine kinase, thymidylate kinase and pyrimidine diphosphate kinase. Reported FIAU-treated patient findings include severe lactic acidosis, massive macro- and microvesicular steatosis in liver biopsies, and enlarged, irregular mitochondria on electron micrographs; mitochondrial toxicity is suggested as the key mechanism. In vitro HepG2 data (excluded from the human claim) showed dose-dependent increases in lactic acid production, elevated ATP content, micro-/macrovesicular steatosis, and enlarged mitochondria with higher cristae density after FIAU exposure.

corrected_record.extra_details: Focal molecule PA is the specific GPR43 agonist (S)-2-(4-chlorophenyl)-3,3-dimethyl-N-(5-phenyl thiazole-2-yl) butanamide; HBx plasmid transfection is the challenge/cotreatment; n=5-6. Correct original-paper PA identity and model scope. Retain bounded inflammatory/redox mechanism with source challenge context; in-vivo applicability is unestablished.

decisions.reason: Original paper identifies a peptide-enriched calf spleen extract, not butyl gallate. A mixture has no unique small-molecule structure. Correct material description remains in reviewed/raw records. Quarantine the confirmed false molecule association after original-paper recovery; retain underlying protective, negative and mechanistic observations as material-level evidence.

corrected_record.support_text: 24-h CSEI incubation significantly caused MMP loss in hepatocellular carcinoma cells, indicated by augmented green fluorescence (JC-1 monomers) and reduced red fluorescence (JC-1 aggregates) (P < 0.01).
corrected_record.assay_and_readout: JC-1 staining—red/green fluorescence ratio reflecting mitochondrial membrane potential dissipation
corrected_record.biological_model_context: HepG2 and SMMC-7721 hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines
corrected_record.result_value: MMP loss (increased JC-1 monomers/green, decreased aggregates/red)
corrected_record.extra_details: Focal molecule CSEI (butyl gallate); ratio of red to green fluorescence reported (n=6); specific dose not reported.
